page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mixed profile. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core stress-ng performance of 787.09 and weak multi-core stress-ng performance of 3134.25. However, Geekbench results show strong single-core performance of 2114.0 and average multi-core performance of 6323.0. Memory bandwidth is average for small cached blocks at 411.75 GB/sec but drops to weak levels for large uncached blocks, registering 35.68 GB/sec read and 25.08 GB/sec write.

Given the high memory capacity relative to compute power, this server is suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance CPU execution. It is well-suited for caching layers, text processing, and lightweight software compilation. However, it is less optimal for database operations, high-throughput static web serving, or medium-to-large language model inference, where benchmarks indicate weak to poor performance. The shared CPU architecture offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-heavy development and testing environments.
description: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 4 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs and 48.0 GB of RAM, providing a generous 12.0 GB of memory per core. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance relies on its high memory-to-CPU ratio to support memory-intensive tasks. Benchmark data indicates a clear tradeoff: while Geekbench single-core and text processing scores are strong, raw CPU stress-ng performance and uncached memory bandwidth are weak to poor due to the shared CPU allocation. Consequently, database operations, static web serving, and large-scale LLM inference show lower throughput. This server is best utilized for memory-heavy but compute-light workloads, such as caching, text processing, and lightweight software compilation, offering a cost-effective profile for resource-dense, non-CPU-bound environments.
